# Tenant isolation test

The rule is `tenancy` points 7 and 8 (ADR 0239). Gen already writes one test per service,
`.stackra/tests/tenant-isolation.int.test.ts`: it runs the compiled migrations and `assertRowSecurity` with
`tenantIsolationOptions()`, which checks every owned table's policies and runs a two-tenant probe. You write the other
half: your actions and queries, called as tenant B, see nothing of tenant A.

## Where row-level security is real

PGlite, the memory database driver and the Testcontainers container's default user (a superuser) all bypass row-level
security. A "tenant B cannot read A" test on any of them passes whatever the policies say, so it proves nothing.

- Name it `<subject>-isolation.int.test.ts`. It runs in `test:int`, on Postgres (`usePostgres`), never in the unit tier.
- Arrange rows as the container's user (`runAsTenant` with a factory). Run every call under test as the service role,
  `tenantIsolationOptions().role`, which has no BYPASSRLS: `set local role` inside one transaction.
- Every read under test goes through `TenantIsolationService.withTenant(actor, work)`, which sets `app.tenant_id` for
  the transaction. That is what the pipeline does.
- `stackra validate --repository` fails a unit-tier test that imports `assertRowSecurity` or `tenantIsolationOptions`
  (rule `isolation-tier`).

## Example

The full pattern, with the action pipeline and a testing module, is notify's
`services/realtime-presence/src/modules/presence/__tests__/member-scope-isolation.int.test.ts`. The core of it:

```ts
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import type { Actor } from "@stackra/contracts";
import { usePostgres } from "@stackra/database/testing";
import { TenantIsolationService } from "@stackra/tenancy/node";
import { fakeTenantId, runAsTenant, tenantActor, tenantIsolationOptions } from "@stackra/tenancy/testing";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "@stackra/testing";
import { OrderFactory } from "#modules/orders/database/factories/order.factory";
import { Order } from "#modules/orders/models/order.model";

const postgres = usePostgres({
  migrationsDirectory: fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../../.stackra/migrations", import.meta.url)),
});

/** The role the service connects as: no superuser, no BYPASSRLS, so the policies decide. */
const { role } = tenantIsolationOptions();

/** Runs `work` as the service role, in one transaction. */
function asService<T>(work: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  return postgres.database.transaction(async () => {
    await postgres.database.em().execute(`set local role "${role}"`);
    return work();
  });
}

/** The orders `actor` sees, read as the service role under the tenant the service sets for it. */
function ordersOf(actor: Actor): Promise<Order[]> {
  const tenancy = new TenantIsolationService(postgres.database);
  return asService(() => tenancy.withTenant(actor, () => postgres.database.em().find(Order, {})));
}

/** Empties the tables, then gives the service role (no login, no BYPASSRLS) the schema's tables. */
async function prepare(): Promise<void> {
  const em = postgres.database.em();
  await em.execute(`truncate table "orders"."orders" cascade`);
  await em.execute(
    `do $$ begin if not exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = '${role}') then create role "${role}" nologin nobypassrls; end if; end $$`,
  );
  await em.execute(`grant usage on schema "orders" to "${role}"`);
  await em.execute(`grant select, insert, update, delete on all tables in schema "orders" to "${role}"`);
}

describe("orders tenant isolation", () => {
  const a = fakeTenantId();
  const b = fakeTenantId();

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await prepare();
    // Arranged as the container's user; each row names its own tenant.
    for (const tenantId of [a, b])
      await runAsTenant(tenantId, () => OrderFactory.new().create({ tenantId }));
  });

  it("shows each tenant only its own row", async () => {
    const seen = await ordersOf(tenantActor(b));
    expect(seen.map((order) => order.tenantId)).toEqual([b]);
  });

  it("returns no row without a tenant", async () => {
    // No withTenant on purpose: app.tenant_id is unset, so the policy matches nothing.
    expect(await asService(() => postgres.database.em().find(Order, {}))).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

Add one case per action or query: as tenant B, a get, update or delete of A's row is `not_found` and A's row is
unchanged. Cross-tenant is always `not_found`, never `permission_denied`. If the read without a tenant returns rows,
the policy or `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is missing: fix the migration, not the test.
